newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-AVALANCHE BEAT RED WINGS TO CLINCH DIVISION AGAIN.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-AVALANCHE BEAT RED WINGS TO CLINCH DIVISION AGAIN.

text.p: It was such a big game, the league warned the nice hockey players not to fight.

Adam Deadmarsh scored on the power play and shorthanded as the Stanley Cup champion Colorado Avalanche clinched their second straight Pacific Division title with a 4-2 win over the Detroit Red Wings Sunday in a penalty-filled game played with memories still fresh of last season's bloody playoffs.

The Avalanche improved to 3-0 against the Detroit this season, but it was the first time Colorado right wing Claude Lemieux and Draper played against each other since the playoffs, when Lemieux broke Draper's jaw and other facial bones by slamming him into the boards from behind.

"Tonight was very physical," said Deadmarsh. "There's a lot of penalties for them and for us. Our speciality teams were a big factor for us. We knew it was going to be a big game, it was hyped up a bit. It was an exciting game and it was like the playoffs. Both teams played very intensely."

"You know when you get the league sending in a supervisor talking to both coaches before the game it shows you what the league thinks of the game," said Colorado coach Marc Crawford. "They know it's going to be a big one and obviously, the refereeing is tight as we see anything called all year."

"It was a chippy game, power plays basically carried the game, but it was a good game," said Red Wings centre Steve Yzerman. "We took some dumb penalties, but both teams did. I'm disappointed we lost, but hard-fought playoff type games are great for your team."
Sergei Fedorov's power-play goal 69 seconds into the final period lifted Detroit into a 2-2 tie, but Chris Osgood could not make it stand up.

Keith Jones tallied a power-play goal 5:33 into the third period to break the tie for the Avalanche, who have won two straight after a season-high three-game winless streak. Jon Klemm added an empty net goal.
Brendan Shanahan also scored a power-play goal for the Red Wings, who are 7-2-5 in their last 14 games and fell seven points behind first-place Dallas in the Central Division.
Fedorov has nine points in his last seven games.
Shanahan has 44 goals including a league-leading 20 on the power play.
In Chicago, Tony Amonte registered his second hat trick of the season and the fourth of his career as the Blackhawks withstood a furious rally for a 5-4 victory over the New York Islanders.
Alexei Zhamnov had a goal and three assists and Eric Weinrich also had three assists for Chicago, which extended its unbeaten streak to 2-0-2 and sent the Islanders to their third loss in four games.
Chicago held a 5-3 lead with 5:12 remaining when an apparent goal by New York's Zigmund Palffy, who scored twice, was disallowed.
At Washington, Peter Bondra beat the first-period buzzer to cap a three-goal first period and help the Capitals to a 5-3 victory over the Hartford Whalers.
Phil Housley, Calle Johansson, Michal Pivonka and Steve Konowalchuk also scored for Washington.

Bondra was on the left wing when he streaked into the left faceoff circle and smoked a slapshot past Sean Burke just before the buzzer for the end of the first period sounded. The play withstood video replay and gave the Capitals a 3-1 edge.
The Capitals crept within one point of the Whalers and Montreal for seventh place in the Eastern Conference and forged ahead of Tampa Bay for ninth.
Nelson Emerson scored twice on the power-play and set up Kevin Dineen's man-advantage goal for the Whalers.
At Tampa Bay, Wendel Clark and Steve Sullivan each had a goal and an assist and Felix Potvin turned aside 39 shots as the Toronto Maple Leafs handed the Lightning their third straight loss, 3-1.
Mats Sundin made it 3-0 just over four minutes into the third period with his team-leading 37th goal.

Potvin, who lost his shutout bid when Brantt Myhres tallied with 59 seconds to go in regulation, stopped 29 shots over the first two periods. Toronto broke a five-game winless streak but is 3-1-4 in its last eight.
In Dallas, Mike Modano had a goal and an assist as the Stars extended their unbeaten streak to five games (3-0-2) with a 6-2 victory over the Pittsburgh Penguins.
Petr Nedved had a goal and an assist for the slipping Penguins, who are 1-7-3 in their last 11 games. Pittsbugh centre Mario Lemieux aggravated a hip flexor and did not play.
In Anaheim, Dave Gagner's power-play goal with 13:17 left in regulation lifted the Calgary Flames into a 2-2 tie with the Mighty Ducks, whose club-record unbeaten streak reached 11 (6-0-5).

Robert Reichel had the other Calgary goal. Joe Sacco had a goal and assisted on Sean Pronger's tally for the Ducks, who moved into a tie with Phoenix and St. Louis for fifth place in the Western Conference.
